summary: Round 4, test review, scoped to the delta since ac0c80177469. BOTH round-3 minors are genuinely fixed and I measured the fixes rather than accepting them. (1) The burned-epoch test now kills BOTH mutants I named, and each fails on the COUNT assertion exactly as claimed: fold-the-checkpoint-and-keep-walking lands at 55 requests against the 15 bound, probe-deleted-outright at 52, and in both runs it is the ONLY failing test in 298 -- so this test is the sole killer for that branch. The sentinel is gone and the fixture needs no state production cannot reach. I also checked that the property the sentinel used to pin has not been lost: neutering the offsets merge in crossFromCheckpoint still fails this test (among five). (2) The fifteen imports are actually removed; they were dead, which compilation proves, so nothing any test observes changed. (3) The restored takeoverCost javadoc is accurate against the helper as it now stands: the literal 1 is checkpointEveryDeltas on the 7-arg start, the 4-arg start it warns about really does install CHECKPOINT_EVERY_DELTAS, terms/entries/one-measured-takeover all match the body, and LocalSequencer.commit is unbatched so entries commits are entries deltas. (4) The corrected baseline is measured-true, not transcribed: forcing crossFromCheckpoint to return false reproduces exactly 29 total at one prior term (gets 18, lists 3, stats 4, puts 4) and 284 at sixteen (gets 243, lists 18, stats 19, puts 4), matching both the ChainReplay comment and the suite javadoc. (5) Rules 4-5 across the delta: the only assertion change is the burned-epoch one, and it is strictly stronger -- an added absolute count plus an offset that a full replay no longer satisfies for free, since the walk stops before the deltas are read. No existing assertion was loosened. Round-2 finding M4.9-R2-T6 is closed: an off-by-one that starts the checkpoint hop one entry late is killed by theDELTASAfterTheCheckpointAreReplayed, and one that starts it three early by aCheckpointSittingEXACTLYOnTheBarrierIsUsed. Two minors remain, one with a named surviving mutation. Tree restored, staged diff unchanged at 7781de47, ./gradlew test green.

findings.title: The test named for a RUN of burned epochs has exactly one, and a probe that fires only on the first arithmetic step survives the whole build
findings.why_not_blocking: The mechanism the delta was asked to pin -- that the arithmetic branch probes at all, and that the walk stops rather than folding and continuing -- IS pinned, and I measured both mutants dying on the count assertion. What is unpinned is the repetition of an already-pinned probe, on a rarer shape than the one the test covers. review.md: not a defect in what the delta claims, so it goes in the commit body or a row rather than another round.
findings.failure_scenario: A store outage spans two consecutive failovers, burning epochs N and N+1 before either leader writes its CONTINUE. Epoch N+2 takes over and replayAncestry enters the arithmetic branch twice. A later refactor -- or the flag mutant measured above -- leaves the checkpoint probe firing only on the first arithmetic step, so the walk steps past epoch N-1's checkpoint unread and replays every entry of every ancestor transitively. The suite is fully green: 298 tests, BUILD SUCCESSFUL, because the only test covering that branch has exactly one burned epoch and the first probe is the one that hits. Recovery is back to O(all commit-log entries ever written) on precisely the correlated failure neverOpened's javadoc names, and nothing reports it -- the offsets still come out right.

findings.title: isLessThanOrEqualTo(15L) carries four requests of unforced slack against an actual 11 that is stable, and contradicts the exactness argument fifteen lines above it
findings.detail: MEASURED: the bounded path costs StoreCounts[puts=0, gets=3, lists=3, stats=5] = 11 total, and isEqualTo(11L) is green across three --rerun-tasks runs, so exactness IS stable here -- the fixture is a fresh MemoryBinStore with a frozen clock and a single-threaded recover(). The bound therefore admits four requests of room on the ONLY test covering the arithmetic branch. The same file, fifteen lines above, argues the opposite for its sibling: 'EXACT, like the failover test's counts and for the same reason: an inequality leaves room a regression can live in', and asserts isEqualTo(18L). HONEST QUALIFICATION, because a weak-test claim without a surviving mutation is an opinion: I could not produce a mutation that both fits inside the four-request slack AND survives the suite. The two I tried -- a redundant GET per warm checkpoint probe in CheckpointCursor.newest (+1 here, 11 to 12) and a hop starting three entries early (+3) -- are each killed by aCheckpointSittingEXACTLYOnTheBarrierIsUsed's isEqualTo(18L). So the slack is not hiding anything today; it is room on a branch whose only guard is this assertion, and the file's own stated principle says to close it.
findings.why_not_blocking: No demonstrated surviving mutation inside the slack, and the two mutants this assertion exists to kill die at 55 and 52 against 15 with a margin of forty. Tightening to isEqualTo(11L) is a one-token change and is permitted, but per review.md fixing a minor is usually wrong -- the next round's surface is the prose the fix adds.
findings.failure_scenario: A change lands that adds up to four requests to the bounded burned-epoch crossing -- a redundant probe, a defensive re-GET of the pointer, a hop start off by a few entries. The assertion reads 12, 13, 14 or 15 against a bound of 15 and stays green, so the regression is invisible on the only test covering the arithmetic branch. It is caught today only because a SIBLING test's isEqualTo(18L) happens to cover the same request families on the CONTINUE branch; a regression confined to the arithmetic branch -- the branch this test exists for, and which no other test reaches -- has four requests to live in. That is the path M5's 300 plugin nodes run against R15's ~1 LIST/s ceiling.
